thought.text: The diff only shows differences in trailing slashes on directory entries (an artifact of unzip's list display format), and the `Basic` symbolic link. Let me normalize and verify, and further confirm that all the key resources referenced by index.html are being delivered.

reasoning_content:
The diff output shows that the filesystem matches the zip, but the zip entries have a trailing slash appended to the directory names (a formatting artifact caused by the way unzip -l outputs its list), whereas the entries on the filesystem side don't have a trailing slash. The only real difference is the `Basic` symlink (line 2: "Basic" exists in the filesystem). In other words, the contents match completely: 201 zip entries vs. 202 filesystem entries (201 + the Basic symlink).

Let me normalize and verify: strip the trailing slash from the zip entries, and exclude the "Basic" symlink from the filesystem entries. Then take the diff again.

action.command: sed 's|/$||' /tmp/zip_entries.txt | grep -v '^$' | sort -u > /tmp/zip_norm.txt; grep -v '^Basic$' /tmp/fs_entries.txt | sed 's|/$||' | sort -u > /tmp/fs_norm.txt; diff /tmp/zip_norm.txt /tmp/fs_norm.txt && echo "FS MATCHES ZIP EXACTLY (only extra entry: Basic symlink)"; echo; echo "=== symlink target check ==="; ls -la /var/www/html/examples/; readlink -f /var/www/html/examples/Basic
